subject.title: [Feature]: Add gateway-side circuit breaker for unhealthy sessions after consecutive failures

question: Should OpenClaw add a first-class session-health circuit breaker, and if so what permanent contract should own failure taxonomy, persisted receipt fields, recovery actions, and defaults?
rationale: The remaining work is not a simple bug repair because it would introduce session-state semantics, possible config/default surfaces, and operator recovery behavior that can intentionally pause or rotate existing sessions.

options.title: Design unified session health
options.body: Approve a single session-health contract with receipt fields, thresholds, recovery actions, tests, and docs before implementation.

options.title: Keep narrower guards only
options.body: Decline a general breaker for now and rely on the existing idle-timeout, retry-limit, tool-loop, and compaction-specific guards.

options.title: Track a narrower follow-up
options.body: Split out one concrete source-reproduced failure mode, such as non-idle no-progress attempts, and defer persistence/UI/auto-rotation.

recommendation.title: Design unified session health
recommendation.body: Approve a single session-health contract with receipt fields, thresholds, recovery actions, tests, and docs before implementation.

likelyOwner.reason: steipete co-owned the adjacent idle-timeout breaker merge and is the best available routing candidate for cross-cutting runtime/product policy.
